picks.name: NVIDIA
picks.setup: 18-day flat base under the 4 Sep high, tightening into the right side
picks.why: Highest readiness in this scan. NVDA has based for 18 sessions under its $234.76 high (4 Sep); across the base, daily ranges are ~40% narrower and volume ~35% lighter than the run into the pivot, and the last four sessions held a tight $227–233 band. The base is a little longer than the clean 5–15 day window, and as a $5.6T name it tends to move slower — a +10% target may take longer than on a mid-cap.
picks.trim: Round number $250 sits about two-thirds of the way to target — trim 25% there.

picks.name: Delta Air Lines

Biggest caveat: earnings 9 Oct, before the trade has room to work — per the playbook, half size at most into the print, or wait and trade the reaction.

catalysts.name: Accenture plc
catalysts.what: Fiscal Q4 revenue $18.68B (+6% y/y) beat the $18.03B estimate; EPS $3.29 beat the $3.18 estimate. Shares surged as much as ~22% intraday and closed up ~16% — the company's best single trading day on record — on a strong FY2027 outlook and a record $85B of new bookings heading into the new fiscal year.

catalysts.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
catalysts.what: Fiscal Q4 revenue $54.23B (+379% y/y) beat the $51.07B estimate; adjusted EPS $33.42 beat the $31.61 estimate, on surging AI-driven cloud memory demand. Guided fiscal Q1 revenue to ~$61.5B and EPS to ~$38.15, well above the ~$57.0B/$35.40 Street view.

catalysts.name: Synopsys, Inc.
catalysts.what: 2026 Investor Day: raised FY2027 revenue guidance to ~$11.15B (~15% y/y growth, ~44% non-GAAP operating margin); disclosed a $1B+ multi-year AWS deal licensing its silicon IP for the Nitro/Graviton/Trainium chip lines, plus a revenue-sharing OpenAI partnership to build an AI model for chip design. Shares jumped as much as ~13% on 1 Oct.

catalysts.name: Target Corporation
catalysts.what: HSBC upgraded to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $190 from $125 (~21% above the current price), citing a foot-traffic-driven comp-sales recovery (+3.8%) and room for margin expansion toward ~6%. Shares rose about +2% on the upgrade; little follow-through since.
